scope: Use one SQLite read snapshot for each task catalog response and the task portion of attention; freeze process-local job observations before durable reads and reuse them for counts, filters, row projection and epoch validation.
prior_behavior: Root metadata, conversation summaries, body matches and leases opened separate connections. Concurrent append/restore, reply replacement or job completion could produce a response combining data from different commits or job observations.

cases: Archived header combined with a newly appended QUEUED turn
Old-keyword search mismatches the header snapshot after a reply replacement
Running count/filter/row use changing process-local jobs

coverage: Restoration and append stay in one commit
Caller-owned connection is neither closed nor committed
Concurrent writer can take worker lock and commit while read preserves old snapshot
One connection without runtime initialization or full payload hydration
Read-only optional metadata tables and legacy roots
408 roots cross summary/search batch boundaries consistently
Real HTTP append and body replacement during reads
backend.connection_evidence: A searched catalog response is asserted to open exactly one Store connection and observe jobs exactly once. A distinct writer thread acquires the application worker lock and commits while the reader is active.

frontend.note: Response structure and interaction code remain unchanged. Four real browser journeys cover the affected API consumers; no redundant full JavaScript-only run was needed.

browser.isolation: Disposable synthetic local fixtures; real browser history pagination, body search, attention, archive/restore and existing read-failure recovery. No real model or business systems.

limits: Consistency is per request, not a persistent snapshot across multiple pages or refreshes.
Process-local jobs and SQLite are separate sources; one observation is reused and epoch-checked, without claiming an atomic memory/database transaction.
Only the task portion of attention shares this snapshot. Workflows, daily plans and alerts keep their own read boundaries.
Queries remain header projections and bounded text excerpts but still scan eligible history; no new million-record performance claim.
Caller-provided connections must already belong to the intended read transaction. Helpers do not begin, commit or close a caller transaction.
Read-only compatibility covers optional name/archive/favorite tables, not absent base conversation/cancellation structures.
Local 1.3.0 candidates have not been published or reinstalled in a fresh environment.
